messages.content: Let’s finish the Chicago arts weekend hotel. We arrive around midday Friday, fly home Monday in the middle of the afternoon, and need one room for three nights. The concert is Saturday, the museum entry is Sunday morning, and we’ll need the hotel to keep our luggage Monday after checkout.

I found two workable final quotes for two adults. The Loop option is a short walk from the museum; the Uptown option is walkable to Saturday’s concert. I’m checking the mandatory fees, transportation, cancellation, deposit, and Monday luggage terms so the displayed rates do not obscure the real totals.
Good. Please compare the complete amounts, not just the nightly prices.

The Loop hotel is $219 per night for three nights. Its $769 total includes $657 room charge and $112 in taxes and mandatory charges. The Uptown hotel displays $184 per night, but its initial $661 quote excludes a mandatory $30 nightly facility fee. Adding $90 makes its complete lodging total $751.
So Uptown is still $18 less. What would we spend getting around from each? We’re comfortable using the train.

For the Loop hotel, allow about $25 total for two adults: $15 for the O’Hare train trips and about $10 for Saturday’s round trip to the concert area. The museum is walkable. For Uptown, allow about $45: the same airport allowance plus roughly $30 for Friday, Sunday, and Monday trips to central Chicago. The concert is walkable from there.
That puts lodging plus transit at $794 downtown and $796 in Uptown, correct? What about storing two bags Monday?

Correct before luggage storage. The Loop hotel stores checked-out guests’ bags at no charge until 6:00 p.m. Monday. Uptown charges $5 per bag and requires collection by 4:00 p.m., so two bags bring that comparison to $794 for the Loop and $806 for Uptown.
The Loop is looking better. Are both rooms refundable, and do either of them take a large deposit now?

The Loop rate can be canceled without charge through 6:00 p.m. local time Wednesday before arrival; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. It charges a $256 first-night deposit when booked. Uptown’s deadline is earlier, 11:59 p.m. Tuesday, and a later cancellation forfeits the full three-night stay. Its deposit is $214 at booking.
What bed types are attached to those prices?
The Loop quote is for one standard queen room. Uptown’s quoted rate is also for one standard queen; a king is available there for another $12 per night before tax.

For this room, since my spouse and I are sharing and haven’t asked for separate beds, the queen is the right choice. That shouldn’t be assumed for some other room if we were booking for additional people.
Understood. I’ll keep the queen only for the room the two of you are sharing and treat any other room’s sleeping arrangement separately.
Choose the Loop hotel. The small price advantage, better cancellation terms, free bag storage, and Sunday walk are worth more than being near the concert for one night.

The Loop hotel is selected: one standard queen room for two adults, Friday check-in through Monday checkout, three nights, with a complete lodging total of $769. Estimated CTA spending is $25 for the two of you, making the lodging-and-local-transit estimate $794.
Please put the exact booking details together so I can confirm them without missing the deposit or bag note.

Booking details: one standard queen room for Elena Ruiz and one accompanying adult; check in Friday after the midday arrival and check out Monday; three nights; $769 including all mandatory charges and taxes. A $256 deposit is due at booking. Free cancellation ends Wednesday at 6:00 p.m. Chicago time, after which one night plus tax is charged. On Monday, leave both bags with the front desk after checkout and retrieve them by 6:00 p.m.; there is no storage fee. The hotel is walkable to Sunday morning’s museum entry, with Saturday concert transportation budgeted separately.
